summary: Builds the placeholder shown when a list or area has nothing to display, with an optional icon, a title, a description, and an action area.
purpose: Gives empty screens a consistent, friendly look. Other screens place these parts where content would normally appear.
why: Likely reason: a shared empty-state look keeps the app consistent. The code does not state this directly.
how: It imports the variant helper and the style helper. It builds an outer box, then header, icon holder, title, description, and action area parts. The icon holder has a plain style and a boxed style chosen by a variant setting. It exports the parts at the end.
inputs: Content placed inside each part, an optional variant setting for the icon holder, and style overrides.
outputs: Components that render an empty-state block. Nothing is stored.
risks: Display only. The main risk is a wrong variant name leaving the icon unstyled. Each part also needs to be used inside the parts that contain it.
debug: If the placeholder looks wrong, check the matching part in this file and the screen that places it. If the icon box is plain, check the variant passed in.
